name: Benzoyl peroxide
summary: A core acne topical that lowers bacterial burden and helps prevent antibiotic resistance when paired with topical or oral antibiotics.
good: Acne regimens that need antimicrobial support and resistance suppression.
bad: Very sensitive or already-overtreated skin unless introduced carefully.
clinicalPearls: It is one of the most useful acne drugs because it helps both treatment and stewardship.
mechanism: Oxidative antimicrobial action reduces Cutibacterium acnes and helps unclog acne-prone follicles.
indications: Inflammatory acne, combination acne regimens, and antibiotic-resistance mitigation.
interactionNotes: Often paired with topical clindamycin or other acne regimens to improve the resistance profile.

warnings: Irritation, dryness, bleaching of fabrics, and barrier disruption are common practical issues.

originalFields: Mechanism
Oxidative antimicrobial action reduces Cutibacterium acnes and helps unclog acne-prone follicles.
Typical uses
Inflammatory acne, combination acne regimens, and antibiotic-resistance mitigation.
Key cautions
Irritation, dryness, bleaching of fabrics, and barrier disruption are common practical issues.
Important interactions
Often paired with topical clindamycin or other acne regimens to improve the resistance profile.
Pearl
It is one of the most useful acne drugs because it helps both treatment and stewardship.
Best use case
Inflammatory acne, and specifically as the resistance-preventing partner for any topical or oral antibiotic.
Speed of response
Relatively fast for inflammatory lesions — visible reduction in active pustules/papules within 2–4 weeks.
Irritation risk
Moderate to high, dose-dependent; dryness, peeling, and occasional allergic contact dermatitis. Lower concentrations (2.5–5%) are often just as effective as 10% with less irritation.
Pigmentation relevance
Not pigment-targeted; irritation itself can trigger PIH in susceptible skin, so concentration matters.
Barrier effects
Can be drying and barrier-disruptive, especially at higher concentrations or with frequent use.
Wash-off vs leave-on
Both exist — leave-on gels/creams for spot or regional treatment, wash-off cleansers for broader or maintenance use with less irritation.
AM / PM use
Either — photostable, so timing is flexible; often used in the morning if a retinoid is used at night.
Combination compatibility
The single most important co-therapy ingredient in acne — always pair with a topical or oral antibiotic to prevent resistant C. acnes strains.
